21-120.name: Differential and Integral Calculus
21-120.rationale: Differentiation, integration and their mathematical applications are central.

21-122.name: Integration and Approximation
21-122.rationale: Integration, approximation, series and numerical mathematical methods are central.

21-127.name: Concepts of Mathematics
21-127.rationale: Mathematical proof, logic, sets, functions and elementary number theory are central.

21-150.name: Mathematics and the Arts
21-150.rationale: Mathematical ideas and artistic/literary interpretation jointly shape the course; neither subject should be discarded.

21-241.name: Matrices and Linear Transformations
21-241.rationale: Linear algebra covers matrices, vector spaces, linear transformations and eigenvalues.

21-259.name: Calculus in Three Dimensions
21-259.rationale: Multivariable and vector calculus, derivatives and integrals are central.

21-266.name: Vector Calculus using Matrix Algebra
21-266.rationale: Matrix-based multivariable calculus is the explicit mathematical subject.

21-268.name: Multidimensional Calculus
21-268.rationale: Rigorous multivariable calculus and vector analysis are the explicit subject.

21-269.name: Vector Analysis
21-269.rationale: Honors real/vector analysis emphasizes proofs, topology, differentiation and integration.

21-325.name: Probability
21-325.rationale: Probability theory, distributions, conditioning and limit theorems are central.

21-425.name: Probability and Martingales
21-425.rationale: Rigorous probability and martingale theory are central.

36-218.name: Probability Theory for Computer Scientists
36-218.rationale: Probability foundations and random-process theory support subsequent computing applications.

36-225.name: Introduction to Probability Theory
36-225.rationale: Probability theory covers distributions, conditioning and limit theorems.

36-226.name: Introduction to Statistical Inference
36-226.rationale: Statistical inference includes estimation, testing and regression.

36-235.name: Probability and Statistical Inference I
36-235.rationale: Calculus-based probability and statistical inference are the explicit subject.

36-236.name: Probability and Statistical Inference II
36-236.rationale: Probability distributions, estimation and multivariate statistical inference are central.

36-303.name: Sampling, Survey and Society
36-303.rationale: Sampling methods and survey design are studied alongside their social, political and institutional history; the course has both mathematical and human-context substance.

36-401.name: Modern Regression
36-401.rationale: Statistical regression and data-model assessment establish the mathematical/statistical subject.

36-402.name: Advanced Methods for Data Analysis
36-402.rationale: Advanced statistical inference and modeling methods are central, despite overlap with predictive learning applications.
